subject: snail
pitch: A garden snail on an adventure. A glossy spiral shell striped in caramel, chocolate and cream, a soft grey-green body with a pebbly texture and a slimy shine, two long eye stalks with little black eyes and two short feelers below. A tiny ladybird hitches a ride on top of the shell.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a TS module using the SDK for a garden snail model, thinking through realistic proportions like shell diameter around 4-5cm to keep the scale grounded.

For the structure, I'm sketching the joint hierarchy starting with hips as the root joint near the ground, then figuring out how to build the spiral shell using either a sweep along a spiral path or a simpler lathe-based dome shape.

For the painted texture, I'm planning a paint function that computes spiral stripe bands using the angle around the shell's axis combined with the radius, creating caramel/chocolate/cream coloring that follows the shell's natural spiral pattern.

Now I'm sketching the actual lathe profile points for the shell dome shape, making sure the outline sweeps from the axis outward to the rim and back without self-intersecting, then considering whether to add a separate spiral whorl ridge as a tube swept along a spiral path sitting on the dome's surface, adjusting its radius to roughly track the dome's curvature.

I'm turning to the overall body construction: the foot will be a swept shape following a path from head to tail, with the shell placed on top toward the back, and I'm starting to lay out joint placements for the creature's structure.

Still defining joint chain...

For the eye stalks, I'll chain them as curved tubes rising from the head joint, using a catmull path that angles up and forward, with the eye sphere placed at the tip of each stalk bone.

I'm also planning shorter feelers below the stalks, swept thinner with rounded tips, and thinking through how the head itself connects to the body as an ellipsoid shape.

For the mouth I want a jaw that can open, so I'm adding a separate small jaw joint as a child of the head joint, referencing the body chain's joint names to figure out which one represents the head.

Now I'm working out the loft stations along the body path, placing tapered width/height values from tail to shoulders so the shell sits nestled into the top of the body near the midpoint, and making sure the lowest station height keeps the body's bottom touching the ground plane.

Rethinking shell scale — a 0.034 radius dome makes the shell too wide compared to the body, so I'll shrink it to roughly 0.02 radius for a more proportional 0.04 diameter, 0.03 height shell relative to the body's 0.09 length.

I'm defining the lathe profile points for the shell's curved spiral silhouette and positioning where it sinks into the body, then setting up a paint function that computes spiral stripe coloring based on each point's position relative to the shell's center.

I'll import paint, mottle, countershade from the library, then use mottle for a pebbly grey-green texture with a darker shade variant, since I can't fake specular shine without actual lighting support.

For the ladybird, I'm positioning a small scaled sphere near the top of the shell's dome, calculating an approximate surface point by working through the dome's radius-height profile to place it convincingly riding on the shell.

For the spots I'll call surface().around() with default bounding-box center and place each at given azimuth/elevation angles, guarding against null hits. The ladybird assembles from a red body sphere, a small black head sphere, and black dot spheres on top.

Now I'm working out how to seat the ladybird onto the shell surface by sticking a hit point with the normal aligned to Y, attaching it to the shell's bone so it rides with the body rather than floating independently. I'm positioning the black head as a small sphere offset slightly above and forward of the ladybird's attachment point using the same hit reference, nudged along its coordinates.

Then I'm building the eye joints: spherical black eyeballs mounted at the tips of eye stalks, with tiny white glint spheres offset locally forward and up for highlight, and considering a slightly larger black bulb at the stalk tip for a more natural look. I'm also starting to lay out the stalk chain branching from a head joint positioned near the front of the head, planning the curve path for the stalks using a catmull spline from that origin point.

For feelers I'll use a tentacle role with a thinner, slightly darker sweep, skipping tip spheres to keep things simple. I'm weighing whether to add a jaw joint for a small mouth near the head front, but given the snail isn't a typical creature with upper/lower jaws, I'm leaning toward skipping it to avoid unnecessary risk.

I'm now adjusting the body's loft proportions so the tail and midsection sit flatter against the ground, tweaking width and height values at each station to keep the belly sink within an acceptable tolerance.

Working out the five profile stations along the body path—tail, rear, mid, neck, and head—with widths and heights that taper naturally, then mapping these to a catmull-rom chain where the final point becomes the head tip joint.

I need a root joint before the chain starts, so I'm adding a "hips" joint at the tail position, treating it as the parent even though it's redundant with the first chain point, since chains may require an explicit root. Then I'm positioning the shell as a separate bone attached near the "mid" joint, sinking slightly into the body's back and extending slightly wider than the body at that point.

For the shell's dome height and the ladybird's placement, I'm computing the nearest surface point near the top rather than hardcoding coordinates. I'm considering adding a spiral ridge sweep across the shell to suggest a subtle whorl, choosing a center point and pitch so it rises from the shell's base radius up toward the apex, though the painted stripe pattern may already convey this well enough on its own.

Rather than fighting the geometry mismatch to get a ridge that tracks the dome's radius profile exactly, I'm deciding to skip the physical ridge and rely on the surface paint for the spiral shell look. For the paint function, I'm computing the angle and radial distance of each point relative to the shell's center axis using atan2 and hypot on the x/z offsets.

Writing spiral paint logic...

I'm also confirming the lathe orientation and segment settings for smoothness, then starting the body paint with a mottled caramel/light pattern using small-scale noise and moderate contrast.

Now I'm planning the ladybird's red body with black spots and black head, checking that the shell bottom sits above the body's lowest point for proper grounding, and working out eye placement using the stalk tip joints with black sphere eyes and small white glint highlights positioned slightly forward and up from the eye frame.

Defining color palette constants...

Setting up the module imports and build function structure, defining the hip joint and the catmull-spline body chain for the snail with named segments from tail to head.

I'm reconsidering the joint hierarchy to avoid zero-length bone issues, repositioning the hips root at the mid-body station and letting the body chain run from tail through head, then extracting the head tip as a typed joint. Now I'm starting the loop to build the pair of eye stalks on each side.

Now I'm adding feeler chains off the head joint with their own sweep geometry, then setting up a jaw joint positioned forward and down from the head to attach a box-shaped mouth piece.

Working out the shell paint pattern...

I'm defining the shell's lathe profile as a revolved outline forming a spiral cone shape, checking the point sequence for the lathe to make sure the silhouette closes properly at the tip.

Now I'm working out how to place a ladybird on the shell by finding the nearest surface point above it and attaching a small sphere body there, figuring out embed depth so it sits realistically sunk into the surface without floating or disappearing.

Actually, maybe skip the head detail and focus on placing spots around the ladybird's surface using angular coordinates from its center.

Placing spot positions...

It's a bit risky near the dome edges but should work fine for placing spots on the ladybird surface. For the body texture, I'm planning to add a mottle paint effect plus a scatter of small bumps across the body loft to give it a pebbly feel.

I'm thinking through how to scatter tiny sphere bumps across the body surface while filtering out points that would end up buried under the shell -- using the normal direction and z-position to exclude areas covered by the dome, so the pebbly texture only shows on the exposed underside and sides of the body.

Simplifying the filter to just check n.y and y-position under the shell overhang, good enough. I'll paint pebbles with BODY_D color and make sure array types are properly declared for the catmull point arrays before finalizing the loft station code.
